newsitem.title: UK: IBCA assigns long-term A rating to BPI-SGPS.
newsitem.headline: IBCA assigns long-term A rating to BPI-SGPS.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Thursday it had assigned long-term A and short-term A1 ratings to BPI-SGPS, the holding company for the Banco Portugues de Investimento group.

"At the same time, the long-term ratings for the three banks within the group, Banco Portugues de Investimento (BPI), Banco Fonsecas & Burnay (BFB) and Banco de Fomento e Exterior (BFE), are removed from RatingWatch with positive implications," IBCA said in a statement.

The short- and long-term ratings of BPI, the investment bank, were affirmed at A1 and A, while the long-term ratings for the commercial banking operations within the group, BFB and BFE, were each upgraded to A plus, IBCA said.
Their short-term ratings were also affirmed at A1.
The rating agency said BPI and BFB were both controlled by BPI-SGPS. BPI recently acquired a 51 percent stake in BFE, previously controlled by the government.
BPI-SGPS acquired a further 14% stake in BFE and a bid to acquire the outstanding shares in BFE was announced on 24 September 1996.
BFE is an investment and development bank which, in turn, controls a retail commercial bank, Banco Borges e Irmao (BBI).
"The acquisition of BFE has more than doubled the size of the BPI group and as a result its position within Portugal's banking industry has changed significantly," said IBCA.
IBCA said the Portuguese authorities would view the group on an integrated basis and that state support would be available for the commercial banking operations of the group.
"BFE represents a good fit for BPI," the statement said. "The combined strengths of BPI and BFE position the group at the forefront of Portugal's investment banking sector."
It said BFB and BBI operate in similar market segments, with little geographical overlap and considerable opportunities for cooperation.
"The enlarged BPI will be well placed to compete and the outlook for the group is favourable," IBCA said.
